extracted.intended_audience: education researchers (PIs and Co-PIs) preparing preproposals and full proposals for the Spencer Foundation Large Research Grants program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation/eligibility criteria for applying to the Spencer Foundation Large Research Grants on Education (field-initiated research grants, $125k–$500k, 1–5 years). Covers preproposal and full proposal content, formatting, budgets, eligibility, and submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program fit: contribution to improvement of education
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must be education research that will contribute to the improvement of education, broadly conceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation seeks rigorous, intellectually ambitious and technically sound research that is relevant to the most pressing questions and compelling opportunities in education and that develops new foundational knowledge that may have a lasting impact on educational discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-initiated scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This program is 'field-initiated' — proposals are not in response to a specific request for a particular research topic, discipline, design, method, or location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may propose work across disciplinary and methodological perspectives (e.g., education, anthropology, philosophy, psychology, sociology, law, economics, history, neuroscience). The Foundation is open to diverse methods and topics; fit is judged on intellectual merit and relevance rather than topic-specific solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour, intellectual ambition, and technical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be rigorous, intellectually ambitious, and technically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation values creative and open-minded scholarship, deep inquiry, and robust questions. Proposals should demonstrate methodological rigor appropriate to their approach and show capacity to answer the research questions posed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly contribution / significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must explain how the field will be different as a result of this research and what new knowledge or contribution to the improvement of education is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preproposal and full proposal narratives require clear statements of significance and the scholarly contribution; this includes situating the work within existing scholarship and explicating the conceptual/theoretical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological appropriateness and detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must describe research design, sampling, recruitment, data collection methods, and data analysis procedures appropriate to the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full proposals should include information on sample/case definition and selection, research design and context, description of key constructs/measures/data sources, data collection procedures, and procedures for data analysis. The Foundation welcomes quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, ethnographies, design-based research, participatory methods, historical research, and multi-source/longitudinal approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include a timeline indicating proposed start/end dates and key project events/milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline (up to 1 page) should reflect major activities listed in the proposal narrative. Proposed project duration may be up to 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget size and funding tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget totals must be between $125,000 and $500,000 and applicants should choose one of three tiers: $125,000–250,000; $250,001–375,000; $375,001–500,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation will distribute awards across tiers and strongly encourages applicants to request the amount that best fits the project rather than automatically seeking the highest amount. In past cycles, lower tiers sometimes had better odds of funding; applicants should design budgets well-suited to project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost (IDC) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets may include up to 15% indirect cost charges (IDC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcontract budgets may also include 15% IDC, but subcontract IDC should not be included in the main budget total when calculating overall IDC for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable budget categories and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable expenses include Salaries, Benefits, Other Collaborator, Travel, Equipment and Software, Project Expenses, Other, and Subcontracts; each expense should be added with a budget narrative describing that expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full proposal budget form contains pulldown categories and line-item choices. Provide a budget justification (chart/table preferred). Subcontracts require separate subcontract budget forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed projects may not be longer than 5 years in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design project scope, timeline, and budget to fit within a maximum 5-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI and Co-PI eligibility (degrees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators and Co-Principal Investigators must have an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate students may be part of the research team but may not be named PI or Co-PI on the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution willing to serve as the administering organization; the Foundation does not award grants directly to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include non-profit or public colleges, universities, school districts, research facilities, or other non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status (or equivalent outside the U.S.). Ensure the administering organization is willing to accept and manage the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and currency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are accepted from the U.S. and internationally, but all proposals must be submitted in English and budgets must be proposed in U.S. Dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare application materials in English and present budget figures in USD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on active Spencer research grants per PI/Co-PI
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may only hold one active research grant from the Spencer Foundation at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PI/Co-PI may apply for a new Spencer grant while they have an active grant only if the active grant will end before the anticipated start date of the new project. This restriction does not apply to the administering organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may not submit more than one research proposal or preproposal to the Spencer Foundation at a time across certain programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies to Small Grants, Large Grants, Racial Equity Research Grants, and Research-Practice Partnership Program. If a PI/Co-PI has a preproposal or proposal under consideration in any of these programs, they must wait until a final decision is made before submitting a new one. Exception: Vision Grants (with conditions that projects be distinct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preproposal format and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal must be a single PDF, double-spaced, no smaller than 12-point font; preproposal narrative ≤1250 words; include PI last name and request ID at top of first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preproposal components to include in one PDF: narrative (≤1250 words with recommended sub-section word counts), up to two pages of references (not counted toward word count), one-page team description (not counted), one-page draft timeline, up to two-page draft budget with justifications. Name the file with PI last name and request ID; if resubmission prefix with 'Resubmission'. The preproposal does not require an institutional signatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preproposal narrative required elements and recommended word counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal narrative must address: description of problem/issue and significance (recommended 250 words); research question(s) (100 words if needed); theoretical/conceptual positioning within scholarship (400 words); summary of research design (400 words); and scholarly contribution (100 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the end of the preproposal narrative include a word count in parentheses. Use citations and include up to two pages of references (not counted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preproposal supplementary documents and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal may include up to two pages of references, a one-page team description, a one-page timeline, and up to two pages for budget and budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supplementary pages do not count toward the 1250-word preproposal narrative. Use chart/table format for budget justification if preferred. The Foundation does not require an official university sign-off at preproposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal narrative content and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposal narrative (by invitation) may not exceed 5000 words and must include project description, central research questions, significance, rationale (literature and conceptual framework), detailed methods, participants, instruments, and analysis plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include procedures for sample/case selection, research design and context, description of key constructs/measures/data sources, data collection and analysis procedures, and a short description of dissemination plans. Put the reference list after the narrative in the same PDF (references not counted toward 5000-word limit). Use double-spacing, 12-point font, and include page numbers. Include the word count in parentheses at the end of the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and trajectories of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should thoughtfully consider and describe plans regarding the trajectories of the project’s findings, implications, and potential effects including how knowledge may be shared and utilized across the field, in practice, policy making, or with broader publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While traditional dissemination (conferences, publications) is expected, the Foundation encourages other forms aimed at impacting policy, practice, or public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team description and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals must include a project team document describing roles, responsibilities, and knowledge base of PI, Co-PIs, and supporting researchers, and how the team will work together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document should articulate each team member's contribution, relationship to research site (if applicable), and learning opportunities for team members. This document should not exceed 800 words and be double-spaced in 12-point font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If resubmitting, applicants must indicate resubmission status and upload a 1-page explanation of how the proposal was revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the preproposal stage prefix file name with 'Resubmission,' and in full proposal include the one-page response describing revisions made since prior submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and document conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must follow formatting rules: double-spaced, 12-point font, include word counts in parentheses, include PI last name and project title on first page, include page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and figures can be included sparingly; text in tables/figures will not count toward the word limit, but any tables/figures must be described or explained in the narrative (and that explanatory text does count). Submit single PDF with all required components in specified order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum vitae / profile requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PI must upload current CV to their online profile with a 10-page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The My Profile page is the applicant's online account for applying, reviewing, and grantee reporting. Co-PIs must create/update profiles and be connected to the proposal for the full proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI agreement and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be asked to acknowledge that they have read, understood, and agree to comply with the Spencer Foundation's policy guidelines on the responsible and ethical use of generative artificial intelligence (AI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy outlines responsible and ethical AI use across Foundation operations and programs; applicants must acknowledge compliance when submitting in SmartSimple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars are expected to follow the highest ethical and professional standards of their fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the Foundation's statement of ethics and professional expectations and ensure research procedures, consent, data handling, and reporting adhere to disciplinary and institutional norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and selection process expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposals are reviewed and applicants will receive light feedback; invitation to submit a full proposal is by invitation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the preproposal to demonstrate fit, significance, and feasibility; a strong preproposal increases chances of invitation. Full proposal review will require more detailed methodological and budgetary justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural steps and account management
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must register and submit through Spencer's online portal (SmartSimple); the PI should complete the My Profile page and upload CV; draft applications can be saved and edited before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If someone else completes the form on behalf of the PI, the PI should register and provide their username/password to the assistant. For full proposals, Co-PIs must have accounts and be connected to the proposal in the system.
